text:
monitoring-bot: [ALERT] apac3 control-plane apiserver QPS surge detected -> increased 5xx and 429s. Auth-proxy returning 502/503 for some requests; provisioning API timeouts visible. Routing controller reporting backpressure. :warning:

maya (oncall): joining. what's the blast radius? are GPU node launches failing or just slow?

monitoring-bot: scope: apac3 control-plane. Provisioner API calls timing out (client-side 120s). Dedicated GPU slot allocations pending; autoscaler requests queued. No node hardware faults reported.

kevin (infra): confirmed. provisioner is getting 429s from apiserver, retries piling up -> retry storm. backlog=62 allocations. Autoscaler can't reconcile. This will delay bringing up burst GPUs.

sam (runtime): impact: model-serving routes in apac3 are tripping circuit-breakers and falling back to smaller/quantized variants. Customer latency and error-rate spikes in telemetry. Recommend immediate partial traffic shift for critical realtime routes to na-east1/eu-west1.

elena (support): seeing customer tickets about console errors (500) when changing routing or viewing cluster state. Marking P1 for customers on Dedicated.

maya (oncall): immediate actions: 1) pause non-essential config writes/rollouts to reduce write QPS 2) throttle CI and internal canaries targeting apac3 3) scale provisioner horizontally + add client-side backoff 4) staged traffic-shift for critical routes. I'll own coordination.

kevin (infra): scaling provisioner from 3 -> 8 replicas now, and temporarily bumping K8s client QPS for provisioner service account. Adding exponential jitter to retries. Will also add ephemeral quota guard for CI.

sam (runtime): preparing routing plan. Proposal: stepwise shift 0% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with health windows and automatic rollback. Critical-prod routes only initially.

maya (oncall): pausing rollouts with:
```
redwoodctl rollouts pause --region=apac3 --reason="control-plane QPS surge"
```
Pausing canaries and non-critical autopromote jobs.

monitoring-bot: provisioner backlog -> 62 -> 27 in 4m after scaling + backoff. apiserver 429 rate down but still above baseline. auth-proxy errors reduced but present.

sam (runtime): starting 10% shift for route: /v1/realtime/critical -> na-east1. Monitoring error-rate and p50/p95.

elena (support): posting interim status to impacted customers: mitigation in progress, suggested workaround: point console/API to alternate region or retry.

kevin (infra): noticing periodic etcd leader elections correlated with bursts of config writes earlier. That amplifies availability impact. For now, keep write flood controlled. Investigating control-plane disk IO & network.

monitoring-bot: backlog -> 12. apiserver 5xx trending down. Routing controller backpressure metrics decreasing. Console errors down 65%.

sam (runtime): advancing to 50% after 8m. No immediate regressions. Holding at 50% for 10m window.

maya (oncall): keep rollouts paused and CI throttled for at least 30m post-backlog. If apiserver 5xx < baseline for 10m and backlog == 0, we can unpause gradually.

kevin (infra): root cause preliminary: internal CI canaries + provisioner retries created a client-side amplified write/read storm against apiserver. Fixes: client-side exponential backoff, lower default retry concurrency, and short-term CI quotas. I'll open a follow-up changelist.

elena (support): updating customers: we'll send a final all-clear after 1h of stable metrics and invite enterprises to a post-incident summary.

monitoring-bot: provisioner queue cleared. apiserver 429/5xx back to baseline. auth-proxy errors minimal. routing backpressure resolved.

maya (oncall): marking mitigation achieved. Next steps: post-incident RCA doc (owner: kevin), add automated routing fallback when control-plane error signals detected (owner: sam), and implement CI quotas (owner: infra). Thanks all :heart:

kevin (infra): will follow up with permanent provisioner rate-limit and client-mitigation + RFC for control-plane write-smoothing.

sam (runtime): adding a playbook entry: if control-plane QPS spike in a region, automatically drain noncritical routes and initiate staged failover to healthy regions.

elena (support): will close customer notices after 60m stable.

monitoring-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: apac3 control-plane write/QPS surge -> provisioning backpressure mitigated.
